Definition: probably from the base of G5490; a huge fish (as gaping for prey):--whale.
BiblicalUsage: Kētos is the huge fish, the great sea creature that gapes for its prey. Matthew 12:40 puts it at the centre of Jesus' own sign: as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly, so the Son of man would be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jesus chose this sign on purpose, because the fish that swallowed Jonah and gave him back is the picture of a death that does not keep its dead.
